processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik narrated: It reached him that Umar ibn al-Khattab assessed the blood money (diyyah) for the people of the towns, making it for the people of gold one thousand dinars, and for the people of silver twelve thousand dirhams. Malik said: The people of gold are the people of Sham and the people of Egypt, and the people of silver are the people of Iraq. And Yahya narrated to me from Malik that he heard that the blood money is paid over three years or four years. Malik said: Three years is most beloved to me of what I have heard in that. Malik said: The agreed-upon matter among us is that camels are not accepted from the people of the towns in blood money, nor gold or silver from the people of the tents, nor silver from the people of gold, nor gold from the people of silver.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa'id: That Marwan ibn al-Hakam wrote to Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan that an insane person was brought to him who had killed a man. Mu'awiyah wrote to him: 'Make his family pay the blood money and do not retaliate against him, for there is no retaliation upon an insane person.' Malik said regarding an adult and a child who together killed a man intentionally: The adult is to be killed, and upon the child is half the blood money. Malik said: Similarly, the free man and the slave who kill a slave - the slave is killed and upon the free man is half his value.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Yahya narrated to me from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Irak ibn Malik and Sulayman ibn Yasar: That a man from Banu Sa'd ibn Layth made his horse run and it trampled upon the finger of a man from Juhaynah, who suffered from it and died. Umar ibn al-Khattab said to those who were accused: 'Will you swear by Allah fifty oaths that he did not die from it?' They refused and were scrupulous. He said to the others: 'Will you swear?' They refused. So Umar ibn al-Khattab ruled that half the blood money be upon the Sa'di people. Malik said: The practice is not based on this.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: And it was narrated to me from Malik: That Ibn Shihab, and Sulayman ibn Yasar, and Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman used to say: 'The blood money for accidental killing is twenty bint makhad, twenty bint labun, twenty ibn labun (male), twenty hiqqah, and twenty jadha'ah.' Malik said: The agreed-upon matter among us is that there is no retaliation between children, and their intentional acts are considered accidental as long as they have not incurred the prescribed punishments and reached puberty. The killing by a child can only be accidental. Thus, if a child and an adult killed a free man accidentally, upon the 'aqilah (family responsible for blood money) of each of them is half the blood money. Malik said: Whoever is killed accidentally, his blood money is wealth, there is no retaliation in it. It is like his other wealth - his debts are paid from it and his bequest is valid in it. If he had wealth such that the blood money would be the amount of one-third of it, then he forgave his blood money, that is permissible for him. If he had no wealth other than his blood money, then one-third of it is permissible for him if he forgave it and bequeathed it.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: Malik narrated to me: That the agreed-upon matter among them regarding accidental injury is that blood money is not obligated until the wounded person recovers and becomes healthy. If a bone of a person is broken - a hand, a leg, or other part of the body - accidentally, and it heals and recovers and returns to its original state, there is no blood money for it. But if it is diminished or there is impediment in it, then there is blood money according to what has been diminished from it. Malik said: If that bone is one for which the Prophet ﷺ specified blood money, then it is according to what the Prophet ﷺ prescribed for it. Whatever did not have specified blood money from the Prophet ﷺ and no sunnah or specified blood money has passed regarding it, then ijtihad is applied to it. Malik said: There is no blood money for wounds in the body if they were accidental, when the wound heals and returns to its original state. If there is impediment or disfigurement in any of that, then ijtihad is applied to it, except for the penetrating wound (ja'ifah), for in it is one-third of the blood money for a life. Malik said: There is no blood money in the munaqqilah (fracture that moves bone) of the body, and it is like the mudihah (wound exposing bone) of the body. Malik said: The agreed-upon matter among us is that if a doctor performs circumcision and cuts off the glans, then the blood money is upon him, and that is from the accidental error which the 'aqilah bears. Whatever error or transgression the doctor makes, if he did not intend it, there is blood money for it.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Ibn Shihab - and it reached him - from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that they both used to say similar to the statement of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab regarding the woman: That she 'equals the man up to one-third of the man's blood money, and when it reaches one-third of the man's blood money, it becomes half of the man's blood money.' Malik said: The explanation of that is that she equals him in the mudihah and the munaqqilah and what is less than the ma'mumah and the ja'ifah and their likes, which would be one-third of the blood money or more. When it reaches that, her blood money in that is half of the man's blood money.

processed_hadiths.english_translation: And it was narrated to me from Malik that he heard Ibn Shihab saying: 'The Sunnah has passed that when a man injures his wife with a wound, upon him is the blood money for that wound and he is not subject to retaliation.' Malik said: That is only in cases of accident, that the man strikes his wife and something happens to her from his striking that he did not intend, such as when he strikes her with a whip and puts out her eye and the like. Malik said regarding a woman who has a husband and children from other than her 'asabah (paternal relatives) or her people: There is nothing upon her husband if he is from another tribe regarding the blood money of her crime, nor upon her children if they are from other than her people, nor upon her brothers from her mother if they are from other than her 'asabah or her people. These are more entitled to her inheritance, while the 'asabah bears the blood money since the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until today. Similarly, the inheritance of the woman's freed slaves goes to the woman's children even if they are from other than her tribe, while the blood money for crimes of the freed slaves is upon her tribe.

وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، أَنَّهُ /27 سَمِعَ /94 ابْنَ شِهَابٍ /94 ، يَقُولُ : " مَضَتِ السُّنَّةُ أَنَّ /20 الرَّجُلَ إِذَا أَصَابَ امْرَأَتَهُ بِجُرْحٍ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِ عَقْلَ ذَلِكَ الْجُرْحِ وَلَا يُقَادُ مِنْهُ " /27 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 : /10 وَإِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ فِي الْخَطَإِ ، أَنْ يَضْرِبَ الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ فَيُصِيبَهَا مِنْ ضَرْبِهِ مَا لَمْ يَتَعَمَّدْ ، كَمَا يَضْرِبُهَا بِسَوْطٍ فَيَفْقَأُ عَيْنَهَا وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِك /12 ، فِي الْمَرْأَةِ يَكُونُ لَهَا زَوْجٌ وَوَلَدٌ مِنْ غَيْرِ عَصَبَتِهَا وَلَا قَوْمِهَا : /10 فَلَيْسَ عَلَى زَوْجِهَا إِذَا كَانَ مِنْ قَبِيلَةٍ أُخْرَى مِنْ عَقْلِ جِنَايَتِهَا شَيْءٌ ، وَلَا عَلَى وَلَدِهَا إِذَا كَانُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ قَوْمِهَا ، وَلَا عَلَى إِخْوَتِهَا مِنْ أُمِّهَا إِذَا كَانُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ عَصَبَتِهَا ، وَلَا قَوْمِهَا فَهَؤُلَاءِ أَحَقُّ بِمِيرَاثِهَا ، وَالْعَصَبَةُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعَقْلُ مُنْذُ زَمَانِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِلَى الْيَوْمِ ، وَكَذَلِكَ مَوَالِي الْمَرْأَةِ مِيرَاثُهُمْ لِوَلَدِ الْمَرْأَةِ وَإِنْ كَانُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ قَبِيلَتِهَا ، وَعَقْلُ جِنَايَةِ الْمَوَالِي عَلَى قَبِيلَتِهَا /10 *
